# Second LC stage and input filter (generated by lc_ac.py)

Bridge output network, load 700 ohm (400 V / 0.57 A). Gvd = V_tab / V_sw (duty to output), Zo = open-loop output impedance at the tab (no control). Peaks searched in 100-1000 Hz (main LC: 3 mH with the electrolytics) and 1.5-100 kHz (second stage; in Gvd it shows no separate peak, it is buried under the main LC's roll-off, so it is read in Zo). Hvu = second-stage ripple attenuation V_tab / V_uc at 50 / 100 kHz.

| Variant | ESR per electrolytic (ohm) | main LC peak: f (Hz), Gvd (dB) | Zo peak low: f (Hz), ohm | Zo peak high (2nd stage): f (Hz), ohm | Hvu 50 kHz | Hvu 100 kHz |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 0.1 | 292, +9.9 | 299, 20.5 | 5772, 3.42 | 0.012 | 0.005 |
| A | 0.5 | 289, +9.1 | 296, 18.7 | 7267, 2.84 | 0.049 | 0.024 |

| B | 0.5 | 279, +8.5 | 289, 15.9 | 26707, 6.38 | 0.716 | 0.303 |

| C | 0.5 | 276, +7.9 | 286, 16.1 | 17642, 5.82 | 0.420 | 0.191 |

Python model hvnet.py against ngspice: worst relative deviation 2.22e-08 over 10 Hz-300 kHz.

Input filter (L101 33 uH, C101 47 uF on B_P, 2 x 47 uF on UIN; PSU 0.3 ohm + 1 uH): output impedance peak seen by the bridges, against the bridges' negative input resistance V^2 / P = 616 ohm at 300 W (Middlebrook: the peak must stay far below it).
